title: Update on Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Project
what_it_is: Update on Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Project

sections.label: Parliament questions on HSR costs
sections.summary: Questions ask the Transport Minister about Malaysia's HSR intentions, Singapore's costs and losses, and compensation rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Malaysian government has, through diplomatic channels, confirmed its intention to terminate its bilateral agreement with Singapore to build the High Speed Rail; (b) if so, what are the expenses and losses likely to be incurred by Singapore as a result of the termination; and (c) what are Singapore's contractual rights to seek compensation for these expenses and losses in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the costs incurred for the High Speed Rail (HSR) as of June 2018; (b) what other costs does Singapore continue to incur should a decision be not made by the end of 2018; and (c) should Malaysia decide to call off the HSR, what are the existing compensation clauses to safeguard Singapore's interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether he can provide an update on (i) the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail project, the costs incurred to date and expenses over the next six months and (ii) the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System.

sections.label: Mahathir announces HSR dropped
sections.summary: On 28 May 2018 Dr Mahathir said in a Financial Times interview the HSR Project would be dropped as a final decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: On 28 May 2018, Malaysian Prime Minister, Dr Mahathir, announced in an interview with the Financial Times that the HSR Project would be "dropped", and that it was "a final decision" but that this would take time because Malaysia had an agreement with Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore HSR cost estimate
sections.summary: Preliminary estimates put Singapore Government HSR Project costs above S$250 million by end of May 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Based on preliminary estimates, the total cost incurred by the Singapore Government for the HSR Project has already exceeded S$250 million by the end of May 2018.

sections.label: Diplomatic note on compensation
sections.summary: The BA covers compensation, so Singapore sent Malaysia a diplomatic note on 1 June 2018 seeking clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The BA provides for how compensation is to be dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: This is why we sent a diplomatic note to Malaysia on 1 June 2018 to seek immediate clarification on Malaysia’s position.

sections.label: June and future HSR spending
sections.summary: Singapore incurred over S$6 million in June and will need to spend at least S$40 million more from August to year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In the month of June, we incurred more than S$6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: From August to end of this year, we will need to spend at least S$40 million more.

sections.label: Compensation under BA and law
sections.summary: Compensation is not a penalty, and if Malaysia terminates the HSR Project Singapore will seek compensation under the BA and international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Compensation is not a penalty imposed on the other country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Thus, should Malaysia cause the HSR Project to be terminated, we will deal with the question of compensation from Malaysia for costs incurred by Singapore in accordance with the BA and international law.

sections.label: Toll cuts and shuttle services
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia lowered off-peak tolls at Tuas Checkpoint and increased KTMB Tebrau Shuttle services from 26 to 31 daily, easing congestion while awaiting the RTS Link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Earlier this year, both Singapore and Malaysia lowered the tolls during off-peak hours at Tuas Checkpoint to encourage motorists to travel outside the peak periods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: We also agreed to Malaysia’s suggestion to increase the number of KTMB Tebrau Shuttle services from 26 to 31 daily, which has been implemented since the middle of February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: These measures have helped to alleviate the congestion, but they are not the complete solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: We look forward to the completion and operation of the RTS Link, which will be able to transport 10,000 travellers per direction per hour between Singapore and JB.

sections.label: HSR Project costs and compensation
sections.summary: Singapore continues to incur costs on the HSR Project while fulfilling its HSR BA obligations, and these costs will add to compensation Malaysia would pay if it terminates the project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Meanwhile, we continue to incur costs on the HSR Project as we conscientiously fulfill our obligations under the HSR BA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: These costs will add to the compensation which Malaysia would have to pay, should it cause the project to be terminated.

sections.label: Definition of compensation
sections.summary: Compensation covers expenditures already spent on the project or incurred from fulfilling obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Compensation is for expenditures which are already spent on the project or incurred as a result of fulfilling the obligations.

sections.label: Civil engineering works budget
sections.summary: For civil engineering works, each Government pays for the portion within its own borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: As for the budget for Singapore's portion of the civil engineering work, the agreement is structured this way: for the civil engineering works, each Government takes care of the bill and foot the expenditure of the portion within its borders.
